haileybury.tagline: A boarding school for girls and boys aged 11 to 18 in Hertford, near London, with an education built on curiosity, courage and character.

accreditations.name: ISI (Independent Schools Inspectorate)
accreditations.detail: The official inspectorate for independent schools in England. At its October 2025 inspection Haileybury met all standards, and its academic and co-curricular enrichment programme was judged “a significant strength”.

accreditations.name: IB Diploma Programme
accreditations.detail: The International Baccalaureate Diploma is offered in the Sixth Form. According to the school, its 2026 IB cohort averaged 38.1 points against a global average of 30.88.

accreditations.name: HMC and ISC
accreditations.detail: The Headmasters' and Headmistresses' Conference (HMC) and the Independent Schools Council (ISC), which bring together leading UK independent schools, are among the school's affiliations.

intro: Haileybury is a co-educational boarding school on a 200-hectare campus in Hertford, a short distance from London. Its motto is “Fly High. Fly Fast.”, and the school lives up to it: pupils are encouraged to take on challenges, push their ideas further and think bigger.

The school treats character as part of academic success. Kindness, empathy, integrity and service to others are part of everyday life. Pupils from the UK and from around the world live together in the same boarding houses and learn with and from each other.

The curriculum is broad. Your child builds strong foundations in the early years, then explores their interests and makes more of their own choices as they move up the school. Subject knowledge is combined with project-based work that develops research, teamwork and presentation skills. Technology and AI are used in lessons, but never in place of the close relationship between teacher and pupil.

According to the school, Haileybury pupils go on to leading universities in the UK and around the world. The aim is for them to leave with the values, skills and qualifications they need for life after school.

facts.label: Boarding
facts.value: 13 houses, separate for girls and boys

programmes.title: Lower School
programmes.desc: A foundation stage. Alongside English, maths, science, French, Spanish, Latin, history, geography, theology and philosophy, art, music, drama, and technology and computing, pupils have weekly reading and wellbeing lessons. Workshops in computing, music, drama, art and design technology build their confidence in speaking and their creativity.

programmes.title: Removes
programmes.desc: While continuing the core subjects, your child chooses two specialist pathways, such as Advanced Science and Astrophysics, Computer Science: Programming and AI, Performance Drama, The Greeks, or Literature and Creative Writing. Digital Innovations classes cover the practical and ethical use of AI.

programmes.title: Middles and Fifths: (I)GCSE
programmes.desc: Ten or eleven (I)GCSEs over two years. Maths, English language, English literature, biology, chemistry and physics are compulsory, which keeps every future option open. Your child adds four options from modern languages, humanities, classics, technology and the arts. Exams are taken in the summer term of Year 11.

programmes.title: Pre-Diploma
programmes.desc: A fast-paced one-year course for pupils who join the school in Year 11. Pupils study English and maths plus options in the sciences, humanities and languages, and sit (I)GCSE exams in the summer. It is the first step of a three-year route that continues into the IB Diploma in the Sixth Form.

programmes.title: Sixth Form: A levels
programmes.desc: Pupils usually choose three subjects and study them in depth. In the first year (Lower Sixth) the Academic Extension Programme (AEP) adds academic electives that complement and extend their A level choices.

programmes.title: Sixth Form: IB Diploma
programmes.desc: A broad, internationally recognised programme: six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Alongside them, pupils take Theory of Knowledge, write a university-style Extended Essay and complete Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) projects.

highlights.title: A choice of A levels or the IB
highlights.desc: The school says it is one of only a handful in the UK to offer both in the Sixth Form. Your child picks the route that suits them, supported by a dedicated Sixth Form team, their house team and a personal tutor.

highlights.title: Choosing interests early
highlights.desc: The two Year 9 pathways range from Astrophysics to Creative Writing, so your child can try out what they enjoy before choosing (I)GCSE and Sixth Form subjects.

highlights.title: AI and programming in lessons
highlights.desc: Digital Innovations classes cover the practical and ethical use of AI, and pupils can choose the Computer Science: Programming and AI pathway.

highlights.title: Reading and wellbeing on the timetable
highlights.desc: Reading and wellbeing lessons are part of the weekly timetable from the Lower School through the (I)GCSE years. The school sees reading as a driver of achievement across every subject.

highlights.title: A tutor for every pupil
highlights.desc: A tutor follows your child's academic progress closely, and the house team looks after day-to-day life. The school's pastoral care is built around every pupil feeling known, valued and understood.

highlights.title: Academic Enrichment Group
highlights.desc: Lower School pupils meet once a week outside lessons to practise debating and public speaking, hear guest speakers and prepare a project of their choice for the Haileybury Academic Exhibition Fair.

highlights.title: Room for sport and the arts
highlights.desc: A 25-metre heated pool, sports hall and gym, indoor and outdoor tennis courts, squash and rackets courts, 22 pitches and playing surfaces for everything from rugby to netball, and 5 performance venues.

highlights.title: Values and community
highlights.desc: Kindness, empathy, integrity and service to others run through school life. Pupils take part in community action projects, and the school has partnerships with schools in the UK and abroad.

summerSchool.title: A Summer on the Haileybury Campus
summerSchool.intro: Each summer Haileybury opens its campus to students aged 11 to 17. Your child stays in the school's boarding houses, has lessons in Haileybury's classrooms and labs, joins sport and arts activities in the afternoons, and sees more of England on day trips. There are three courses, chosen by age and English level.

courses.title: English+
courses.dates: 11–24 July · 25 July – 7 August · 4 weeks: 11 July – 7 August
courses.desc: Morning English lessons built around history, science, culture, art and technology (CLIL), then team projects in the afternoon. A warm, busy introduction for children going to a summer school abroad for the first time.

courses.title: Academic English+
courses.dates: 11–24 July · 25 July – 7 August · 4 weeks: 11 July – 7 August
courses.desc: Academic English in the morning through STEM or Arts, Business and Humanities. In the afternoon, one of six expert projects: Coding Academy, World of Science, Design and Manufacturing, Global Entrepreneurs, Filmmaking or a Mini Model United Nations. Your child comes home with their own website, short film or product.

courses.title: Innovation Leaders
courses.desc: An academic programme taught entirely in English for students with advanced English. Creative business development and entrepreneurship in the mornings, STEM projects with AI and new technologies in the afternoons, plus business workshops in the City of London and visits to science venues such as the Royal Institution.

includes: Boarding on campus, with separate houses for girls and boys and mostly single or twin rooms
Three meals a day, with vegetarian, vegan and special diet options and packed lunches on trip days
A sport or arts activity chosen each week: football, tennis, hockey, song and dance, acting, or The Great Haileybury Bake-Off with a professional pastry chef
Evening activities every day from 19:00 to 21:00: outdoor cinema, silent disco, Haileybury's Got Talent and a certificate ceremony on Friday nights
Three full-day trips a week: Cambridge, Oxford or Windsor Castle; London with a boat trip on the Thames; and a theme park such as Thorpe Park
24/7 campus security, a Welfare Manager, a school nurse and a 24/7 emergency line for parents

mpw.tagline: An independent college in London, Birmingham and Cambridge, running GCSE and A level programmes built around each student since 1973.

accreditations.name: ISI (Independent Schools Inspectorate)
accreditations.detail: All three colleges are inspected by ISI. MPW London (May 2025) and MPW Birmingham (October 2025) met all the standards in the inspection framework, and MPW Cambridge (October 2023) met all ISI standards.

accreditations.name: Ofsted: “Outstanding”
accreditations.detail: Ofsted, England's official education inspectorate, rated MPW Cambridge (November 2019) and MPW Birmingham (February 2018) “Outstanding”, its highest grade, in all areas.

accreditations.name: DfE registration, ISA and ISC
accreditations.detail: The colleges are registered with the Department for Education as independent schools, are members of the Independent Schools Association (ISA) and sit under the Independent Schools Council (ISC).

accreditations.name: Top ratings across the group
accreditations.detail: In MPW's words, it is the only education group in England where every college has achieved the highest rating in all areas of its inspection reports.

intro: MPW (Mander Portman Woodward) was founded in London in 1973 by three Cambridge graduates. Today it is one of the UK's best-known independent sixth-form colleges, with colleges in London, Birmingham and Cambridge. Its motto is “Tailored, Not Uniform”: each student gets a programme set up for them.

Students choose their own combination from more than 40 GCSE and A level subjects, over anything from one term to two years. They may have just finished school, or come to MPW to improve their grades. Teaching is exam-focused, classes are small, and many tutors are also exam markers.

The atmosphere is closer to university than school. Students are treated as young adults and call their tutors by first name, but the rules on punctuality and deadlines are firm. Every student has a personal tutor, and guidance on UCAS, Oxbridge and competitive courses such as Medicine is part of the programme.

Around 1,200 students study at the colleges each year, about a third of them from overseas. According to MPW, around two-thirds go on to Russell Group, University of London and specialist universities.

programmes.title: GCSE and IGCSE
programmes.desc: One- or two-year courses for the UK's age-16 exams, depending on your child's age and situation. There are 30 subjects to choose from, from sciences and maths to Mandarin, Latin, Photography and Textiles.

programmes.title: Two-Year A level
programmes.desc: Most MPW A level students take this route. The usual plan is three A levels plus the EPQ (Extended Project Qualification), with the number and mix of subjects adjusted to the student. Subjects are explained at interview, and students can try taster lessons.

programmes.title: One-Year A level
programmes.desc: Self-contained courses that cover the whole syllabus in one year, taught separately from the two-year programme. For students with some sixth-form experience, those changing school, or those adding a new subject for their university application. Expect a fast pace and frequent exam practice.

programmes.title: Transfer at the End of Year 12
programmes.desc: If the first year of A levels hasn't gone to plan, your child can join Year 13 at MPW or repeat Year 12. Subjects and exam boards can be changed where needed, and enrolment stays open until the September term starts.

programmes.title: A level and GCSE Retakes
programmes.desc: For students disappointed on results day. A one-year course if several units need relearning, or a short course starting in January for students who narrowly missed their grades. According to MPW, retake students improve by two grades on average.

programmes.title: Easter Revision
programmes.desc: Intensive revision weeks before exams, open to students from any school. Examiner tutors find the gaps, run past-paper practice and teach exam technique. Available in 30 A level and 16 GCSE subjects at all three colleges.

programmes.title: MPW University Foundation
programmes.desc: A university preparation year in the UK for international students who have finished high school at home. Students follow one pathway (Business and Economics, Engineering, Humanities, Science, or Sports Science and Psychology) alongside academic English.

programmes.title: UAL Foundation Diploma
programmes.desc: A University of the Arts London (UAL) diploma for students aiming for leading art and design degrees in the UK, with portfolio preparation at its centre.

highlights.title: No one-size-fits-all
highlights.desc: More than 40 subjects can be taken in any combination, over anything from one term to two years. Your child's programme is planned around their goals.

highlights.title: Small classes
highlights.desc: MPW guarantees fewer than 10 students in every class. Your child can ask questions easily, and tutors can see exactly where each student is struggling.

highlights.title: Tutors who know the exams
highlights.desc: Tutors hold first-class degrees or doctorates, and many mark A level or GCSE exams in their subject. MPW writes its own course notes.

highlights.title: Exam practice from day one
highlights.desc: Every subject has monthly revision tests. In the exam year, students also sit weekly timed assignments under exam conditions.

highlights.title: Regular updates for parents
highlights.desc: Test and homework marks are on a parent portal throughout the course. On top of parents' evenings, written subject reports go home five times a year.

highlights.title: Personal tutor and university guidance
highlights.desc: Every student has a personal tutor. Support with UCAS, Oxbridge, Medicine and other competitive courses is part of the programme.

highlights.title: Treated as young adults
highlights.desc: Fewer school rules and first names with tutors, but no slack on punctuality or deadlines. Your child gets used to university-style independence before they get there.

highlights.title: Measurable results
highlights.desc: In MPW's 2026 results, 37% of A level grades were A*/A and 62% were A*–B. 85% of Oxbridge offer holders secured their places.

summerSchool.title: MPW Summer School: London and Cambridge
summerSchool.intro: MPW Summer School gives students aged 14 to 17 two weeks to explore an academic subject in English. Your child chooses one of 8 subject streams, joins life-skills workshops, hears university academics speak and learns how UK university applications work. In the school's own words: “Where young minds shine.”

courses.title: London Campus
courses.desc: In South Kensington, home to the museums, Imperial College and the Royal Albert Hall. All 8 streams run here, and Architecture and Art and Design are London only. Students stay at Queen's Gate House next to the college and go on industry trips linked to their subject.

courses.title: Cambridge Campus
courses.desc: In the centre of the famous university city, with 6 subject streams. Students stay at Tripos Court, tour Cambridge colleges and go punting on the River Cam. Four-week students can spend one session in Cambridge and one in London.

includes: One of 8 subject streams: Computing, Robotics and AI; Medicine and Sciences; Physics and Engineering; Business, Finance and Economics; Politics and Law; Psychology and Sociology; Architecture; Art and Design
My Path; My Way life-skills courses, one each week: public speaking, negotiation, persuasion, problem solving, emotional intelligence or media literacy
Weekly lectures by academics from the University of Cambridge and London universities, on topics such as AI and climate change
A 3½-hour University Preparation Workshop on UCAS, Oxbridge applications and personal statements
Guest speakers for each stream, plus industry trips (London) or university tours (Cambridge)
Museums, galleries, theatre, escape rooms, movie nights and karaoke
Single en-suite rooms, House Parents living in, and three meals a day
An awards ceremony on the last Friday, with a certificate and a personal progress report from the stream teacher

oisc.tagline: A private tutorial college and language school in central Oxford, teaching English, GCSEs, A levels and university preparation since 2006.
intro: Oxford International Study Centre (OISC) is a private tutorial college and language school founded in 2006. From its two buildings in Oxford city centre it teaches at every level, from English courses to GCSEs, A levels and university preparation.

English is taught at St Aldates, between Christ Church and the Town Hall, in a 400-year-old red building with beamed ceilings that was once a coaching inn and later a bank. Academic students study at the King Edward Street Academic Centre, three minutes' walk away, in a quiet setting away from the busy language school.

OISC's defining feature is its small classes: academic classes have at most 6 students, usually 3 or 4, and many students take some lessons one-to-one. All English teachers hold the CELTA and several the DELTA, and at least 25 nationalities are in the school in a typical week.
In its April 2026 inspection, the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) judged OISC to “exceed expectations”, its highest grade, for the 8th time in a row.

facts.label: Centres
facts.value: St Aldates and King Edward Street

programmes.title: General English and IELTS
programmes.desc: 20 lessons (15 hours) a week on the Standard course or 30 (22.5 hours) on the Intensive course, across six levels from A1 to C2. Students are grouped by age and level, receive a certificate of attainment, and long-term students usually take IELTS.

programmes.title: One-to-One English
programmes.desc: Flexible one-to-one lessons built around the student's goals. They can be combined with group classes: 20 group lessons plus 5, 10 or 15 individual lessons a week.

programmes.title: Full-Time A Level
programmes.desc: Around 30 subjects to choose from, with about 6 hours a week per subject. Academic English and IELTS support is included for international students, and there is a one-year intensive A level for students whose school qualifications aren't accepted for direct UK university entry.

programmes.title: Full-Time GCSE
programmes.desc: Preparation for the UK's age-16 exams, with 3 or 4.5 hours a week per subject. Classes have at most 6 students, usually 3 or 4, and every student has a personal tutor they meet weekly.

programmes.title: University Foundation in Business
programmes.desc: Modules in Academic English, Maths, Economics, Business and Study Skills. Successful students are guaranteed progression to business, management and finance degrees at around 20 UK universities, including Oxford Brookes.

programmes.title: Oxford and Cambridge Preparation
programmes.desc: All tutors are Oxford or Cambridge graduates. One-to-one or in groups of 2–3: subject tuition, preparation for admissions tests such as ELAT, TSA and LNAT, personal statement feedback and practice interviews.

programmes.title: British Boarding School Preparation
programmes.desc: English plus 3–5 academic subjects and study skills, 20–25 lessons a week. Younger students prepare for Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning, Common Entrance and the ISET, with help choosing a school and interview practice.

programmes.title: Easter Revision
programmes.desc: A level, (I)GCSE and IB in more than 30 subjects, in groups of at most 6 or one-to-one. 2–3 subjects a week, 6 hours of academic work a day, daily study skills seminars and a detailed report at the end.

highlights.title: Very small classes
highlights.desc: Academic classes have at most 6 students, usually 3 or 4, and many students take some subjects one-to-one. Tutors can see where your child is struggling from the first week.

highlights.title: Personal tutor and monthly reports
highlights.desc: Every full-time student has a tutor they meet weekly, who follows both their studies and their wellbeing. Parents receive a progress report every month.

highlights.title: A bridge to UK universities
highlights.desc: A one-year intensive A level or Foundation programme for students whose school qualifications aren't accepted for direct entry. Choosing universities, the personal statement and interview practice are part of the programme.

highlights.title: Academic English included
highlights.desc: International GCSE and A level students get Academic English and IELTS support alongside their subjects at no extra cost.

highlights.title: Oxbridge-educated tutors
highlights.desc: Every tutor teaching students applying to Oxford or Cambridge is a graduate of one of the two universities.

highlights.title: Support for special educational needs
highlights.desc: A dedicated SENCo meets students and parents every week, and flexible exam and timetable arrangements are possible.

highlights.title: Weekly enrichment
highlights.desc: Monday afternoons bring guest lectures, study skills seminars and trips such as Cotswold Wildlife Park, plus lunchtime clubs for debating, guitar and crafts.

highlights.title: Checked and inspected accommodation
highlights.desc: Host families are background-checked, complete regular safeguarding training and are inspected at least once a year. The student residence has single en-suite rooms within walking distance of both centres.

summerSchool.title: 12 Weeks of Summer in Oxford
summerSchool.intro: OISC has run summer programmes in Oxford for about 20 years and has welcomed more than 30,000 students, from 36 countries last summer. Unlike many colleges it accepts children under 14, and adults too. Your child studies with others of the same age and level, and can start on any Monday from mid-June to mid-September and stay from 1 to 8 weeks or longer.

courses.title: English Language & Culture
courses.dates: Mid-June to mid-September 2027; starts every Monday
courses.desc: 20 lessons (15 hours) of English a week, social and cultural activities in Oxford every weekday, and a full-day excursion every weekend. Interactive classes for younger learners; Academic English and IELTS options for adults.

courses.title: English, Culture & Academic Enrichment
courses.dates: Mid-June to mid-September 2027; starts every Monday
courses.desc: Everything in the first course, plus 10 lessons (7.5 hours) a week of A level, IB or (I)GCSE preparation. Your child chooses 1–2 subjects a week, taught in groups of 3–4 or one-to-one.

includes: 20 English lessons a week, in international classes grouped by age and level
Activities every weekday: punting, museum and gallery visits, college tours and treasure hunts
Full-day weekend excursions: London, Bath and Stonehenge, Cambridge
A host family (breakfast and dinner included), or a single en-suite room in the student residence 2 minutes' walk from OISC (ages 14+)
On request and subject to availability, rooms in an Oxford University college for ages 16+
Optional one-to-one Oxford and Cambridge interview preparation or boarding school entrance test preparation

accreditations.name: ISI: “Exceeds expectations”
accreditations.detail: In a three-day inspection in April 2026, the Independent Schools Inspectorate judged OISC to “exceed expectations”, its highest grade, for the 8th time in a row, highlighting safeguarding, pastoral care and flexible courses. ISI is an inspection body authorised by UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI).

accreditations.name: COBIS
accreditations.detail: Accredited member of the Council of British International Schools.

accreditations.name: ISC and AEGIS
accreditations.detail: Member of the Independent Schools Council (ISC) and a member school of AEGIS, committed to the safe guardianship of international students.

accreditations.name: The Tutors' Association, ECIS and more
accreditations.detail: Corporate member of The Tutors' Association and a recognised provider of the European Association of Training Providers; member of ECIS, the European Association for International Education (EAIE), JAOS and the Swiss Group of International Schools.

ef.tagline: An international education company teaching languages since 1965, with English courses, summer camps and university preparation in the UK.
intro: EF (Education First) was founded in 1965 and, with more than 450 schools and offices worldwide, describes itself as one of the world's largest education companies. It has taught English to international students in England for over 50 years and runs 8 schools across the country: London, Oxford, Cambridge, Manchester, Brighton, Bournemouth, Eastbourne and, in summer, Cambridge Clare College.

The EF Method, which EF developed itself, combines classroom teaching, digital materials and everyday use of English. EF makes a clear promise: a student who attends every class and does all the homework moves up one EF level every 6 weeks, or gets extra tuition free.

Students from more than 80 countries study at EF schools. Everyone studies full time, with no evening or weekend classes. Outside lessons, each school's activities coordinator runs trips, events and sport.

University preparation is one of EF's strengths in the UK. Programmes in Oxford and Manchester prepare students for undergraduate study after school, for master's or MBA study after a degree, and for a PhD. According to EF, successful graduates are guaranteed a place at one of its 150 partner universities.

programmes.title: General English
programmes.desc: 26 lessons a week, with four Special Interest Lessons (SPINs) covering speaking, listening, reading and writing. Your child's level is measured with EF SET tests at the start and tracked throughout.

programmes.title: Intensive English
programmes.desc: 32 lessons a week for the fastest progress, with the most Special Interest Lessons in topics such as presentations, academic writing and critical thinking.

programmes.title: IELTS Preparation
programmes.desc: Preparation for IELTS and IELTS Academic, the tests UK universities ask for. Advanced students can also take a 2-week course in Cambridge.

programmes.title: Cambridge Exam Preparation
programmes.desc: Preparation for KET, PET, FCE, CAE and CPE, starting in January, April, June or September. Most EF schools are authorised exam centres, so students sit the exam where they studied.

programmes.title: EF Academic Year Abroad
programmes.desc: A year or semester of English in the UK, at general or intensive pace, with the option to finish with IELTS or a Cambridge exam. Starts in January, April, June or September.

programmes.title: University Foundation Year
programmes.desc: In England, international students with fewer than 13 years of schooling take a preparation year before starting a degree. 9 months (11 for September starts), in one of Business, Science and Engineering, Humanities and Law, Medicine and Pharmacy, or Art and Architecture. In Oxford and Manchester.

programmes.title: Pre-master's and Pre-MBA
programmes.desc: Six months of preparation for a UK master's or MBA: academic English, IELTS, research methods and specialist modules. According to EF, successful graduates are guaranteed acceptance at one of its partner universities.

programmes.title: Pre-PhD
programmes.desc: Six months of preparation for doctoral study with PhD-qualified tutors: thesis proposal, academic publishing and advanced research methods. Successful graduates are guaranteed a PhD place at a partner university.

highlights.title: From a 12-year school system to a UK degree
highlights.desc: Direct entry to UK universities usually expects 13 years of schooling. The University Foundation Year fills that gap for students who finish school after 12 years, as in Turkey. In EF's published results, every graduate won an undergraduate place and 25% went to a top-20 UK university.

highlights.title: Where graduates go
highlights.desc: According to EF, Foundation graduates have been admitted to universities including LSE, UCL, King's College, Bath, Birmingham, Durham and Exeter, and Pre-master's alumni to Oxford, Cambridge, York and Leeds.

highlights.title: A progress guarantee
highlights.desc: Students who attend every class and do the homework move up one EF level every 6 weeks, or get extra lessons free. Progress is measured with EF SET tests and certified at the end.

highlights.title: Sit the exam at school
highlights.desc: Most EF schools in England are authorised Cambridge English exam centres, so your child takes the exam they prepared for in a familiar place.

highlights.title: Schools in the heart of each city
highlights.desc: London is in a historic Victorian building near the London Eye and the South Bank. Oxford is near the university colleges with around 3 acres of gardens. Cambridge has a renovated Victorian building, and Manchester sits next to Platt Fields Park.

highlights.title: An international classroom
highlights.desc: Students from more than 80 countries, in classes averaging 12–15 and never more than 17. Your child uses English every day with classmates from around the world.

highlights.title: Life outside lessons
highlights.desc: Every school has an activities coordinator, with day and overnight trips to places such as Stonehenge, Bath, Oxford, Cambridge, the Lake District, Warwick Castle and Edinburgh, plus evening events and clubs.

highlights.title: What the course includes
highlights.desc: Lessons, a homestay (breakfast and dinner on weekdays, all meals at weekends), digital materials, level tests, a certificate and weekly activities.

summerSchool.title: A Summer in England with EF
summerSchool.intro: EF's UK summer camps are for teenagers aged 13 to 17. Your child can start at any level, on any Monday in June, July or August, for 2 to 4 weeks: English lessons in the morning, then trips and activities in the afternoons and at weekends. EF hand-picks its camp leaders and trains them to work with international teens.

courses.title: Cambridge Clare College
courses.dates: June, July and August; starts every Monday

story.paragraph1: Families and companies looking for international education or innovation programs often had to deal with several providers of uneven quality. We started Robonino to give them one reliable, professional service instead.

Young Engineers is an education brand active in over 100 countries and recognised by the Harvard Graduate School of Education and the European Commission. We also work with Education Advisers, a UK education consultancy, to guide families through school and university placement.

members.name: Tolga Düzenli
members.role: Robonino Founder and UK Education Consultant
members.bio:
I graduated from Hacettepe University with a degree in Computer Engineering in 2011. Having had the opportunity to live in three different countries, I have been based in London since 2018, where I work as a software engineer in the financial sector.

Becoming a father gave me a new perspective on children's development, education and the decisions parents make about their children's future. This interest inspired me to take my first step into children's education in 2024, launching a LEGO and STEM education business in London as a Young Engineers franchisee. I later brought the same educational concept to Turkey, establishing Genç Mühendisler in Adana.

Through Robonino, I now aim to help families in Turkey find the right English language schools and educational programmes for their children. Living in London gives me the opportunity to build direct relationships with UK schools, gain first-hand knowledge of their programmes and understand the local educational environment. I want to use this experience and local insight to help families make informed decisions and find opportunities that match their children's interests and needs.

For me, it is about more than simply recommending a school or a programme. It is about helping families find the right educational experience, one that supports their children's development while giving parents confidence and peace of mind.

members.name: Miray Soylu
members.bio: I live in Istanbul, I'm a lawyer and the mother of a daughter. The care I took in choosing a school where my daughter would feel safe and happy and learn English is the care I bring to the families I guide at Robonino. I travel to London often to get to know schools and programmes first-hand. Together with families, I look at summer school and half-term English programmes that suit their children's interests and needs, and I support them through the application process.

members.name: Cagatay Duzenli
members.bio:
I am an entrepreneur and business owner working in international education, travel and visa consultancy. Based in Adana, Turkey, I have spent years helping students and families explore educational and professional opportunities abroad.

My main areas of expertise include Work and Travel programmes for university students, as well as visa application consultancy for the UK, European countries and the United States. I also operate a Work and Travel business in the US and support families in Turkey who are exploring international language schools and educational opportunities for their children.

As a father of a daughter, I understand the excitement and responsibility that come with making decisions about a child's international education and future. Through Robonino, I aim to help families not only explore the right educational opportunities but also navigate the visa application processes and practical arrangements that make studying abroad possible.

I believe every international journey starts with good planning, reliable guidance and the confidence to take the first step.
